subject: Post-call: Acorn Health - perf split tests + ask on p95/p99 targets
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: John Patel <john.patel@acornhealth.com>, procurement@acornhealth.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 May 2029 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed A/B matrix (Redwood vs Hyperscaler)

Hi John — great to meet earlier. Thanks for walking us through the two workload patterns (short chat queries + longer summarization requests). Quick recap and concrete next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap (from our call):
- Workload mix: 65% short Q->A (~30-80 tokens), 35% long summarizations (~1.5k tokens input, 400-800 token outputs).
- Current baseline: Acorn says their control (HyperscaleCloud managed endpoint) reports p95 ~340ms for short queries and ~1.8s for long summarizations on current infra. Throughput target: 1.2k tokens/sec sustained for the mixed profile.
- Security: SOC2 proofs and a short data flow diagram will be required for procurement.

What we propose next (actionable):
1) Quick A/B bench: Redwood hosted (redwood-standard-1) vs HyperscaleCloud managed endpoint. Goal: measure p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec under two synthetic mixes (short-first and mixed).
2) Test matrix: see attached bench plan (redwood_vs_hyperscaler-bench-plan.xlsx) — includes sample payloads and ramp schedule.
3) Deliverables: CSV with p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization traces, token/sec curves, and sample model outputs for quality spot-checks.
4) Timeline: if you can provide the sample payloads by EOD Wed (attached placeholder acorn_sample_payloads.json), we can run our first smoke A/B by Fri and share a readout next Tue.

Asks from Acorn: please confirm the representative sample size (we usually need ~5k short + 200 long requests to get stable p95/p99), and whether the procurement team needs any formal statement of work before we run the bench.

I also noted a few immediate differentiators to watch for in the results: our prefix/KV-cache hit rates (saves repeated tokens in convo history), continuous batching behavior at 8–16ms bucket windows (keeps latency predictable), and fallback routing to lower-cost quantized variants when memory spikes. We'll call these out explicitly in the readout so you can weigh cost vs tail-latency tradeoffs.

Attachments: acorn_sample_payloads.json, redwood_vs_hyperscaler-bench-plan.xlsx

Next steps (I) I will loop in Marcus and Naomi for the bench ops, (II) John please send sample payloads and any procurement constraints, (III) procurement please flag any compliance docs needed before bench.

Thanks — Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0127
From: John Patel <john.patel@acornhealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acornhealth.com
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 09:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed A/B matrix (Redwood vs Hyperscaler)

Thanks Rishi — that recap is spot on. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Sample payloads: attached are two sets — short_qs_sample.ndjson (3.5k rows) and long_summary_sample.ndjson (220 rows). We withheld PHI; all payloads are synthetic but representative.
- Procurement: we can sign an NDA but don’t need a full SOW to run a non-production bench. Procurement will ask for SOC2 Type II evidence before any production pilot.
- Targets: the p95 numbers you pulled are roughly what we see; we care most about p99 for the short queries (spiky traffic during morning syncs) and p95 for long summaries. Throughput goal remains 1.2k tokens/sec.

One ask from engineering: can you include tokenization-level metrics so our team can validate tokens/sec across different tokenizers (we still use the default tokenizer from HyperscaleCloud).

We expect to have internal signoff to share the payloads this afternoon. If you can run the smoke tests on Friday, that would be great — we can take the readout next week and decide whether to proceed with procurement.

Regards,
John

[Attachment: short_qs_sample.ndjson (NDJSON, 3.5MB)]
[Attachment: long_summary_sample.ndjson (NDJSON, 1.8MB)]
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: John Patel <john.patel@acornhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2029 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap + proposed A/B matrix — bench ops ask

Marcus / Naomi — forwarding Acorn's sample payloads (short_qs_sample.ndjson, long_summary_sample.ndjson). Please treat as customer-sensitive. High priority bench: Redwood hosted vs HyperscaleCloud (we'll ask Acorn for Hyperscale endpoint credentials under ephemeral test token).

Bench goals:
- P50/P95/P99 for short and long profiles
- Sustained tokens/sec curve across a 30min ramp to 1.5k tokens/sec (we want headroom above their 1.2k target)
- Resource utilization (GPU mem, VRAM pressure, kernel stalls) and KV-cache hit rate
- Tokenization parity check (compare token counts on both sides)

Proposed quick matrix (start Friday smoke -> full run Monday if smoke OK):
- Run A: Redwood hosted (opt quantized variant) — 3 concurrency levels (8, 24, 64)
- Run B: HyperscaleCloud managed endpoint (same model family) — 3 concurrency levels
- Run C: Redwood fallback to quantized-low-mem variant under memory pressure (to show graceful degradation)

Please instrument p95/p99 windows and capture 1s and 10s rolling histograms. Generate CSVs with columns: run_id, timestamp, model_variant, concurrency, p50, p95, p99, tokens_per_sec, kv_cache_hit_pct, gpu_util_pct. Drop the raw perf traces in the Drive folder listed in the related_links.

Log any output quality diffs (we'll include a separate quality bucket to flag hallucinations or truncated outputs). Capture at least 200 long outputs for human spot-check.

Let me know immediately if you see any blocker on payload format, tokenizer mismatch, or if additional harness work is needed. I'll coordinate with John for Hyperscale test creds.

-Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: John Patel <john.patel@acornhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2029 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call recap + proposed A/B matrix — bench ops ask

Thanks Rishi — we've reviewed the samples and the bench plan. Quick ops notes and a short schedule so we can manage expectations: 

1) Tokenization parity: Naomi will run a tokenizer pass today to normalize token counts against Hyperscale's tokenizer. If we see >3% variance on long summaries we'll add a normalization step in the analysis.
2) Smoke Friday: Naomi will run a 500 short + 25 long smoke across Redwood-hosted to validate harness and verify kv-cache instrumentation. If smoke looks good we'll schedule the full A/B Monday 00:00-06:00 PT (low customer traffic window).
3) Measurement specifics we will report: p50/p95/p99 (ms), tokens/sec (sustained and peak), 99.9th percentile kernel stall durations, and KV-cache hit %. We'll produce the CSV format Rishi specified and a short slide with cost delta and tail-latency tradeoffs.
4) Hyperscaler comparison caveat: HyperscaleCloud uses aggressive autoscaling at the infra layer which compresses p95 in short windows; we'll run a synthetic spike test to surface how tail-latency behaves under burst traffic (this is where our routing + batching consistency shows benefits).

No blockers from bench harness — we'll post results to the Drive link and ping John when the smoke completes. Marcus

[Attachment: bench-harness-checklist.md (TEXT, 6KB)]
